correctness.rationale: The weighted cycle Lipschitz increments identify Lip₀(C_m(w)) isometrically with Y_w={u∈ℝ^m:∑w_i u_i=0}, sup norm, even when a long edge is redundant; finite duality preserves numerical index. If 2w_i≥W, eliminating u_i identifies Y_w isometrically with ℓ∞^(m−1). Otherwise the dual unit ball is conv of ±restricted coordinate functionals, each exposed by q_i=1, q_j=−w_i/(W−w_i), so McGregor tests cube-hyperplane vertices for a coordinate inside (−1,1). A cube-section vertex has at most one free coordinate. If all weights equal, parity gives precisely even m. For unequal positive weights in genuine-cycle region take maximal a, alternately sign all other weights equal a to residual 0 or a, then sequentially choose opposite sign for each remaining c<a so |r−c|<a; hence a free maximal-weight coordinate |u_i|<1 yields strict index<1. This handles ties, arbitrary positive reals and thresholds, without assuming finite enumeration proves the universal lemma. Independently checked the exact rational vertex predicate on all 1053 weight vectors m=4..6 each coefficient 1..3, 42302 vertices total; finite diagnostic only.
